readiness_words: A data store this workload reaches changes protocol or has no assessed protocol, and its code migration decision is not answered: StackToIT keeps the workload blocked until the customer answers it in the decisions file.
validation_scope: A kubeconform check or a kubectl apply --dry-run of the manifest establishes YAML validity only, not behaviour: it accepts a REQUIRED_ token in a string field, an empty ConfigMap and a Secret that does not exist, and runs nothing; the checklist of the application compatibility contract and an application smoke test on the target are what show that the workload works.

containers.name: checkout-service
containers.image_rebinding: pulled from where the source pulls it (Amazon ECR image public.ecr.aws/aws-containers/retail-store-sample-checkout:1.6.3): decide where the images live on STACKIT, that the cluster can reach the registry, and the pull secret
probes: livenessProbe: exec curl -f http://localhost:8080/health (the ECS health check)
startupProbe: the same check over the start period

env.name: RETAIL_CHECKOUT_ENDPOINTS_ORDERS
env.source: DERIVED: http://${module.orders_service.ecs_service_name} → Service orders port 80 of this manifest set
env.target: http://orders (the Kubernetes Service orders, port 80, written into the ConfigMap by the manifest)
env.work: the ConfigMap of the manifest already holds http://orders, derived from the source (http://${module.orders_service.ecs_service_name} is the name of module.retail_app_ecs.module.orders_service.aws_ecs_service.this, which the draft writes as the Kubernetes Service orders port 80 in the same cluster): nothing to set; apply the manifests of both services into one namespace (the bare name resolves only there; across namespaces write orders.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local) and check that the Service answers

env.name: RETAIL_CHECKOUT_PERSISTENCE_PROVIDER
env.work: set the key in the ConfigMap to the value module.retail_app_ecs.module.checkout_service.aws_ecs_task_definition.this states for container checkout-service (not copied: an environment value can carry a secret under any name); if it names an AWS endpoint, a region or an ARN, give the STACKIT one

env.name: RETAIL_CHECKOUT_PERSISTENCE_REDIS_URL
env.work: the value is not visible statically (a variable or an expression): set the key in the ConfigMap to the value the running service uses

endpoints.source: checkout:80 (the Service Connect alias of port checkout-service in the namespace retailstore.local)
endpoints.target: checkout:80 (the Kubernetes Service checkout, port 80 → container port 8080, in the namespace the manifests are applied into)
endpoints.work: the Kubernetes Service keeps the name and port the clients call: check that they resolve it from their namespace; the Service Connect proxy (its retries, timeouts, TLS and metrics) is not carried

identity.target: open: the decision target.workload.identity (inputs.json) chooses federated_service_account (a Kubernetes ServiceAccount federated to the STACKIT service account of the role), service_account_key (a key of that service account mounted as a Secret) or no_workload_identity
identity.work: answer target.workload.identity for module.retail_app_ecs.module.checkout_service.aws_ecs_service.this; until then the pods run with no identity and every call the application made with the task role module.retail_app_ecs.module.checkout_service.aws_iam_role.task_role fails
manual_steps: answer the input target.workload.identity for module.retail_app_ecs.module.checkout_service.aws_ecs_service.this in inputs.json: with federated_service_account the draft writes the stackit_service_account of module.retail_app_ecs.module.checkout_service.aws_iam_role.task_role, its federated identity provider for the SKE cluster's service-account issuer and the Kubernetes ServiceAccount checkout in the manifest

until then, create a STACKIT service account named after the task role module.retail_app_ecs.module.checkout_service.aws_iam_role.task_role and grant it the role assignments the policies of module.retail_app_ecs.module.checkout_service.aws_iam_role.task_role give (identity.tf lists them as the architect's variable)

federate it to the SKE cluster's service-account issuer for the subject system:serviceaccount:<namespace>:checkout, and apply the ServiceAccount of applications/checkout.templates.yaml (its annotation holds the service account's e-mail) in the namespace of the workload

change the application from the AWS SDK credential chain to the STACKIT SDK, which picks up the projected token: every call the application made with module.retail_app_ecs.module.checkout_service.aws_iam_role.task_role fails until it does

datastores.work: the target stackit_valkey_instance.dependencies_checkout_elasticache_redis_default (Key Value Store, Valkey) speaks the Redis protocol and accepts TLS connections only, so the clients change: the source runs without TLS (transit_encryption_enabled = false), so the scheme redis:// becomes rediss://, the client's TLS option is switched on and the CA certificate of the instance is trusted; check the commands the application sends against the target before the manifest is applied (its credential is no administrator: CONFIG, ACL and MODULE are denied)

code_migration.question: The protocol compatibility of ElastiCache and the target stackit_valkey_instance.dependencies_checkout_elasticache_redis_default is not assessed: has the application's use of it been checked?

options.title: the calls the application makes were checked against the target store and found compatible
a target store that speaks the protocol of the source is wanted instead: the draft is regenerated with it, and the workload stays blocked until then

dns_dependencies.name: the endpoint host of module.dependencies.module.checkout_elasticache_redis.aws_elasticache_replication_group.default (ElastiCache)
dns_dependencies.source: the endpoint host AWS assigns ElastiCache module.dependencies.module.checkout_elasticache_redis.aws_elasticache_replication_group.default when it is applied (not visible statically), answered by AWS DNS (inside a VPC the VPC resolver answers it with a private address)
dns_dependencies.target: the host name the STACKIT instance stackit_valkey_instance.dependencies_checkout_elasticache_redis_default (Key Value Store (Valkey)) publishes, read from the instance and its credential after it is applied; the draft holds no value of it
dns_dependencies.verification: resolve, from a pod of checkout, the host of stackit_valkey_instance.dependencies_checkout_elasticache_redis_default and connect to its port: the draft does not state whether the name resolves to an address the cluster's network reaches, so record the address and that the connection opens

dns_dependencies.name: checkout
dns_dependencies.source: a Service Connect alias in the Cloud Map private DNS namespace retailstore.local (module.retail_app_ecs.aws_service_discovery_private_dns_namespace.this): the clients of the namespace resolve it through the Service Connect proxy of their tasks
dns_dependencies.target: checkout.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local (the Kubernetes Service checkout; checkout from a pod of the same namespace)
dns_dependencies.verification: resolve, from a pod of a client of checkout, checkout and checkout.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local: expect the ClusterIP of the Kubernetes Service checkout (kubectl get service checkout)
